CANICULAR: Pertaining to, or measured, by the rising of the Dog Star. Canicular days, the dog days, See Dog days. -- Canicular year, the Egyptian year, computed from one heliacal rising of the Dog Star to another.
CRITICALNESS: 1. The state or quality of being critical, or of occurring at a critical time. 2. Accuracy in examination or decision; exactness.
CHOLERIC: 1. Abounding with, or producing choler, or bile. Dryden. 2. Easily irritated; irascible; inclined to anger. 3. Angry; indicating anger; excited by anger. "Choleric speech." Sir W. Raleigh. Choleric temperament, the bilious temperament.

COLLECTIVE: 1. Formed by gathering or collecting; gathered into a mass, sum, or body; congregated or aggregated; as, the collective body of a nation. Bp. Hoadley. 2. COTTA: 1. (Eccl.) A surplice, in England and America usually one shorter and less full than the ordinary surplice and with short sleeves, or sometimes none. 2. A kind of very coarse woolen blanket.
COMPREHENSOR: One who comprehends; one who has attained to a full knowledge. [Obs.] When I shall have dispatched this weary pilgrimage, and from a traveler shall come to be a comprehensor, farewell faith and welcome vision. Bp. Hall.
COADUNATION: Union, as in one body or mass; unity. Jer. Taylor. The coadunation of all the civilized provinces. Coleridge.
CONVINCEMENT: Act of convincing, or state of being convinced; conviction. [R.] The fear of a convincement. Milton.
CLOWNISH: Of or resembling a clown, or characteristic of a clown; ungainly; awkward. "Clownish hands." Spenser. "Clownish mimic." Prior. -- Clown"ish*ly, adv. Syn. -- Coarse; rough; clumsy; awkward; ungainly; rude; uncivil; ill- bred; boorish; rustic; untutored.
CACODEMON: 1. An evil spirit; a devil or demon. Shak. 2. (Med.) The nightmare. Dunaglison.
COTYLEDONARY: Having a cotyledon; tufted; as, the cotyledonary placenta of the cow.
CALENDRIC: Of or pertaining to a calendar.
CHANCEL: (a) That part of a church, reserved for the use of the clergy, where the altar, or communion table, is placed. CORDY: Of, or like, cord; having cords or cordlike parts.
COURTIER: 1. One who is in attendance at the court of a prince; one who has an appointment at court. You know I am no courtier, nor versed in state affairs. Bacon. CONCLAMATION: An outcry or shout of many together. [R.] Before his funeral conclamation. May (Lucan).
CYSTIDEA: An order of Crinoidea, mostly fossils of the Paleozoic rocks. They were usually roundish or egg-shaped, and often unsymmetrical; some were sessile, others had short stems.
CUSPIDOR: Any ornamental vessel used as a spittoon; hence, to avoid the common term, a spittoon of any sort.
CYMOPHANOUS: Having a wavy, floating light; opalescent; chatoyant.
COMMUNALISM: A French theory of government which holds that commune should be a kind of independent state, and the national government a confederation of such states, having only limited powers. It is advocated by advanced French republicans; but it should not be confounded with communism.
CHIDINGLY: In a chiding or reproving manner.
CRESTFALLEN: 1. With hanging head; hence, dispirited; dejected; cowed. Let it make thee crestfullen; Ay, and allay this thy abortive pride. Shak. 2. Having the crest, or upper part of the neck, hanging to one side; -- said of a horse.
CENTISTERE: The hundredth part of a stere, equal to .353 cubic feet.
COLLECTIVIST: An advocate of collectivism. -- a. Relating to, or characteristic of, collectivism.
COLLIQUEFACTION: A melting together; the reduction of different bodies into one mass by fusion. The incorporation of metals by simple colliquefaction. Bacon.
CHARCOAL: 1. Impure carbon prepared from vegetable or animal substances; esp., coal made by charring wood in a kiln, retort, etc., from which air is excluded. CIRCUMAGITATE: To agitate on all sides. Jer. Taylor.
CHESSMAN: A piece used in the game of chess.
CAUSALITY: 1. The agency of a cause; the action or power of a cause, in producing its effect. The causality of the divine mind. Whewell. 2. (Phren.) The faculty of tracing effects to their causes. G. Combe.
CLEFT: from Cleave. 1. Divided; split; partly divided or split. 2. (Bot.) Incised nearly to the midrob; as, a cleft leaf. 1. CAPITATIM: Of so much per head; as, a capitatim tax; a capitatim grant.
CAFENEH: A humble inn or house of rest for travelers, where coffee is sold. [Turkey]
CONCILIATION: The act or process of conciliating; the state of being conciliated. The house has gone further; it has declared conciliation admissible previous to any submission on the part of America. Burke.
COMETOGRAPHY: A description of, or a treatise concerning, comets.
CRATE: 1. A large basket or hamper of wickerwork, used for the transportation of china, crockery, and similar wares. 2. A box or case whose sides are of wooden slats with interspaces, -- used especially for transporting fruit. To pack in a crate or case for transportation; as, to crate a sewing machine; to crate peaches.
CRUMPLE: To draw or press into wrinkles or folds to crush together; to rumple; as, to crumple paper. They crumpled it into all shapes, and diligently scanned every wrinkle that could be made. Addison. To contract irregularly; to show wrinkless after being crushed together; as, leaves crumple.
CALORICITY: A faculty in animals of developing and preserving the heat nesessary to life, that is, the animal heat.

CAUDICULA: A slender, elastic process, to which the masses of pollen in orchidaceous plants are attached.
CURB ROOF: A roof having a double slope, or composed, on each side, of two parts which have unequal inclination; a gambrel roof.
CROQUET: 1. An open-air game in which two or more players endeavor to drive wooden balls, by means of mallets, through a series of hoops or arches set in the ground according to some pattern. 2. CASTELLAN: A goveror or warden of a castle.
CARPATHIAN: Of or pertaining to a range of mountains in Austro-Hungary, called the Carpathians, which partially inclose Hungary on the north, east, and south.
CROSSROW: 1. The alphabet; -- called also Christcross-row. And from the crossrow plucks the letter G. Shak. 2. A row that crosses others.
CAREX: A numerous and widely distributed genus of perennial herbaceous plants of the order Cypreaceæ; the sedges.
CHANGEFUL: Full of change; mutable; inconstant; fickle; uncertain. Pope. His course had been changeful. Motley. -- Change"ful*ly, adv. -- Change"ful*ness, n.
CAECIAS: A wind from the northeast. Milton.
CAOUTCHIN: An inflammable, volatile, oily, liquid hydrocarbon, obtained by the destructive distillation of caoutchouc.
CATAPELTIC: Of or pertaining to a catapult.
CUSTOMABLE: 1. Customary. [Obs.] Sir T. More. 2. Subject to the payment of customs; dutiable.
CAGELING: A bird confined in a cage; esp. a young bird. [Poetic] Tennyson.
COULOIR: 1. A deep gorge; a gully. 2. (Hydraul. Engin.) A dredging machine for excavating canals, etc.
CUCKOOPINT: A plant of the genus Arum (A. maculatum); the European wake- robin.
CONNECTIVE: Connecting, or adapted to connect; involving connection. Connection tissue (Anat.) See Conjunctive tissue, under Conjunctive. That which connects. Specifically: (a) (Gram.) CORSET: 1. In the Middle Ages, a gown or basque of which the body was close fitting, worn by both men and women. 2. An article of dress inclosing the chest and waist worn (chiefly by women) to support the body or to modify its shape; stays. To inclose in corsets.
CORNSHUCK: The husk covering an ear of Indian corn. [Colloq. U.S.]
CENTERPIECE: An ornament to be placed in the center, as of a table, ceiling, atc.; a central article or figure.
CREATURESHIP: The condition of being a creature.
CIPPUS: A small, low pillar, square or round, commonly having an inscription, used by the ancients for various purposes, as for indicating the distances of places, for a landmark, for sepulchral inscriptions, etc. Gwilt.

CHAUTAUQUA SYSTEM OF EDUCATION: The system of home study established in connection with the summer schools assembled at Chautauqua, N. Y., by the Methodist Episcopal bishop, J. H. Vincent.

CARLOVINGIAN: Pertaining to, founded by, of descended from, Charlemagne; as, the Carlovingian race of kings.

Formerly called weber.
CANTICLE: 1. A song; esp. a little song or hymn. [Obs.] Bacon. 2. pl. The Song of Songs or Song of Solomon, one of the books of the Old Testament. 3. A canto or division of a poem [Obs.] Spenser. 4. A psalm, hymn, or passage from the Bible, arranged for chanting in church service.
CHUMP: A short, thick, heavy piece of wood. Morton. Chump end, the thick end; as, the chump end of a joint of meat. Dickens.
CROSSBARRED: 1. Secured by, or furnished with, crossbars. Milton. 2. Made or patterned in lines crossing each other; as, crossbarred muslin.

COLONIZATIONIST: A friend to colonization, esp. (U. S. Hist) to the colonization of Africa by emigrants from the colored population of the United States.
CHATOYMENT: Changeableness of color, as in a mineral; play of colors. Cleaceland.
CICLATOUN: A costly cloth, of uncertain material, used in the Middle Ages. [Obs.] [Written also checklaton, chekelatoun.] His robe was of ciclatoun, That coste many a Jane. Chaucer.

CERINTHIAN: One of an ancient religious sect, so called fron Cerinthus, a Jew, who attempted to unite the doctrines of Christ with the opinions of the Jews and Gnostics. Hook.
CURDLE: 1. To change into curd; to coagulate; as, rennet causes milk to curdle. Thomson. 2. To thicken; to congeal. Then Mary could feel her heart's blood curdle cold. Southey. 1. COMMANDRESS: A woman invested with authority to command. Hooker.
CONSUBSTANTIALITY: Participation of the same nature; coexistence in the same substance. "His [the Son's] . . . consubstantiality with the Father." Hammend.
CALUMNIATOR: One who calumniates. Syn. -- Slanderer; defamer; libeler; traducer.
COSMOGONICAL: Belonging to cosmogony. B. Powell. Gladstone.
CHIASMUS: An inversion of the order of words or phrases, when repeated or subsequently referred to in a sentence; thus, If e'er to bless thy sons My voice or hands deny, These hands let useful skill forsake, This voice in silence die. Dwight.

CLUB-SHAPED: Enlarged gradually at the end, as the antennæ of certain insects.

Charnel house, a tomb, vault, cemetery, or other place where the bones of the dead are deposited; originally, a place for the bones thrown up when digging new graves in old burial grounds. A charnel house; a grave; a cemetery. In their proud charnel of Thermopylæ. Byron.

CENTRIFUGAL FILTER: A filter, as for sugar, in which a cylinder with a porous or foraminous periphery is rapidly rotated so as to drive off liquid by centrifugal action.
COCCOSTEUS: An extinct genus of Devonian ganoid fishes, having the broad plates about the head studded with berrylike tubercles.

CHAPMAN: 1. One who buys and sells; a merchant; a buyer or a seller. [Obs.] The word of life is a quick commodity, and ought not, as a drug to be obtruded on those chapmen who are unwilling to buy it. T. Fuller. 2. A peddler; a hawker.
CATAMOUNT: The cougar. Applied also, in some parts of the United States, to the lynx.
CONCIERGE: One who keeps the entrance to an edifice, public or private; a doorkeeper; a janitor, male or female.
CHIROGRAPHY: 1. The art of writing or engrossing; handwriting; as, skilled in chirography. 2. The art of telling fortunes by examining the hand.
CUSPIDATE: To make pointed or sharp. Having a sharp end, like the point of a spear; terminating in a hard point; as, a cuspidate leaf.
CIMOLITE: A soft, earthy, clayey mineral, of whitish or grayish color.

CONTEMPER: To modify or temper; to allay; to qualify; to moderate; to soften. [Obs.] The antidotes . . . have allayed its bitterness and contempered its malignancy. Johnson.

CROISSANTE: Terminated with crescent; -- said of a cross the ends of which are so terminated.
CATENATE: To connect, in a series of links or ties; to chain. E. Darwin.
CONVOCATE: To convoke; to call together. [Obs.] May (Lucan).

COCCOBACTERIUM: One of the round variety of bacteria, a vegetable organism, generally less than a thousandth of a millimeter in diameter.
COMPORTANCE: Behavior; comport. [Obs.] Goodly comportance each to other bear. Spenser.

CONSOLATOR: One who consoles or comforts. Johnson.

CYPRINOID: Like the carp (Cyprinus). -- n. One of the Cyprinidae, or Carp family, as the goldfish, barbel, etc.
COUPSTICK: A stick or switch used among some American Indians in making or counting a coup.
COADJUVANCY: Joint help; coöperation. Sir T. Browne.

COLICKY: Pertaining to, or troubled with, colic; as, a colicky disorder.

CTENOPHOROUS: Of or pertaining to the Ctenophora.

CYMRIC: Welsh. -- n. The Welsh language. [Written also Kymric.]

CASINGS: Dried dung of cattle used as fuel. [Prov. Eng.] Waterland.
CONCLAVE: 1. The set of apartments within which the cardinals of the Roman Catholic Church are continuously secluded while engaged in choosing a pope. 2. The body of cardinals shut up in the conclave for the election of a pope; hence, the body of cardinals. CARUNCULA: 1. (Anat.) A small fleshy prominence or excrescence; especially the small, reddish body, the caruncula lacrymalis, in the inner angle of the eye. 2. (Bot.) An excrescence or appendage surrounding or near the hilum of a seed. 3. (Zoöl.) A naked, flesh appendage, on the head of a bird, as the wattles of a turkey, etc.
COMBOLOIO: A Mohammedan rosary, consisting of ninety-nine beads. Byron.

CRUMMABLE: Capable of being crumbed or broken into small pieces.
CHOANOID: Funnel-shaped; -- applied particularly to a hollow muscle attached to the ball of the eye in many reptiles and mammals.
CRINOIDEA: A large class of Echinodermata, including numerous extinct families and genera, but comparatively few living ones. Most of the fossil species, like some that are recent, were attached by a jointed stem. See Blastoidea, Cystoidea, Comatula.
CRINOID: Crinoidal. -- n. One of the Crinoidea.
CAMARA DOS PARES: Chamber; house; -- used in Ca"ma*ra dos Pa"res, and Ca"ma*ra dos De`pu*ta"dos. See Legislature.
CONSENTINGLY: With consent; in a compliant manner. Jer. Taylor.
CORTICIFORM: Resembling, or having the form of, bark or rind.
CASTAWAY: 1. One who, or that which, is cast away or shipwrecked. 2. One who is ruined; one who has made moral shipwreck; a reprobate. Lest . . . when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway. 1 Cor. ix. 27. Of no value; rejected; useless.
CO-LESSOR: A partner in giving a lease.
CONDONATION: 1. The act of condoning or pardoning. 2. (Law) Forgiveness, either express or implied, by a husband of his wife or by a wife of her husband, for a breach of marital duty, as adultery, with an implied condition that the offense shall not be repeated. Bouvier. Wharton.
CRAMPONEE: Having a cramp or square piece at the end; -- said of a cross so furnished.
CHORDEE: A painful erection of the penis, usually with downward curvature, occurring in gonorrhea.
CLAPPERCLAW: 1. To fight and scratch. C. Smart. 2. To abuse with the tongue; to revile; to scold.
CARBURETOR: An apparatus in which coal gas, hydrogen, or air is passed through or over a volatile hydrocarbon, in order to confer or increase illuminating power. COMMONAGE: The right of pasturing on a common; the right of using anything in common with others. The claim of comonage . . . in most of the forests. Burke.
CUPFUL: As much as a cup will hold.
CHLOROFORM: A colorless volatile liquid, CHCl3, having an ethereal odor and a sweetish taste, formed by treating alcohol with chlorine and an alkali. It is a powerful solvent of wax, resin, etc., and is extensively used to produce anæsthesia in surgical operations; also externally, to alleviate pain. To treat with chloroform, or to place under its influence.
CHAFEWEED: The cudweed (Gnaphalium), used to prevent or cure chafing.
CAUSIDICAL: Pertaining to an advocate, or to the maintenance and defense of suits.
COACTION: Force; compulsion, either in restraining or impelling. Sojth.
COINTENSION: The condition of being of equal in intensity; -- applied to relations; as, 3 : 6 and 6 : 12 are relations of cointension. Cointension . . . is chosen indicate the equality of relations in respect of the contrast between their terms. H. Spencer.
CORPULENT: 1. Very fat; obese. 2. Solid; gross; opaque. [Obs.] Holland. Syn. -- Stout; fleshy; bulky; obese. See Stout.
CLERESTORY: The upper story of the nave of a church, containing windows, and rising above the aisle roofs. Same as Clearstory.
CRAPEFISH: Salted codfish hardened by pressure. Kane.
CONJUNCTIVENESS: The state or quality of being conjunctive. Johnson.
CRUPPER: 1. The buttocks or rump of a horse. 2. A leather loop, passing under a horse's tail, and buckled to the saddle to keep it from slipping forwards. To fit with a crupper; to place a crupper upon; as, to crupper a horse.
CENTRIC: Placed in the center or middle; central. At York or some other centrical place. Sir W. Scott. -- Cen"tric*al*ly, adv. -- Cen"tric*al*ness, n.
CAPELLANE: The curate of a chapel; a chaplain. [Obs.] Fuller.
COIR: 1. A material for cordage, matting, etc., consisting of the prepared fiber of the outer husk of the cocoanut. Homans. 2. Cordage or cables, made of this material.
CUBEB: The small, spicy berry of a species of pepper (Piper Cubeba; in med., Cubeba officinalis), native in Java and Borneo, but now cultivated in various tropical countries. The dried unripe fruit is much used in medicine as a stimulant and purgative.
COLOSSAL: 1. Of enormous size; gigantic; huge; as, a colossal statue. "A colossal stride." Motley. 2. (Sculpture & Painting) Of a size larger than heroic. See Heroic.
CAPRA: A genus of ruminants, including the common goat.
CIRCUMJACENCE: Condition of being circumjacent, or of bordering ou every side.

COOTFOOT: The pharalope; -- so called because its toes are like the coot's.
CONDOLEMENT: 1. Condolence. "A pitiful condolement." Milton. 2. Sorrow; mourning; lamentation. Shak.
CROODLE: 1. To cower or cuddle together, as from fear or cold; to lie close and snug together, as pigs in straw. [Prov. Eng.] Wright. Forby. A dove to fly home her nest and croodle there. C. Kingsley. 2. To fawn or coax. [Obs.] 3. To coo. [Scot.]

CLINKSTONE: An igneous rock of feldspathic composition, lamellar in structure, and clinking under the hammer. See Phonolite.
CARUNCULOUS: Of, pertaining to, or like, a caruncle; furnished with caruncles.
CHOOSE: 1. To make choice of; to select; to take by way of preference from two or more objects offered; to elect; as, to choose the least of two evils. Choose me for a humble friend. Pope. 2. CORRIGENDUM: A fault or error to be corrected.

CIRSOCELE: The varicose dilatation of the spermatic vein.
COEVAL: Of the same age; existing during the same period of time, especially time long and remote; -- usually followed by with. Silence! coeval with eternity! Pope. Oaks coeval spread a mournful shade. Cowper. One of the same age; a contemporary. As if it were not enough to have outdone all your coevals in wit. Pope.
CORBEIL: 1. (Arch.) A sculptured basket of flowers; a corbel. [Obs.] 2. pl. (Fort.) Small gabions. Brande & C.
COUNTESS: The wife of an earl in the British peerage, or of a count in the Continental nobility; also, a lady possessed of the same dignity in her own right. See the Note under Count.
CHURCHMANLY: Pertaining to, or becoming, a churchman. Milman.
CTENOSTOMATA: A suborder of Bryozoa, usually having a circle of bristles below the tentacles.
CADUCOUS: Dropping off or disappearing early, as the calyx of a poppy, or the gills of a tadpole.
CONACRE: To underlet a proportion of, for a single crop; -- said of a farm. [Ireland] A system of letting a proportion of a farm for a single crop. [Ireland] Also used adjectively; as, the conacre system or principle. Mozley & W.
CONFALON: One of a fraternity of seculars, also called Penitents.
COVING: (a) A cove or series of coves, as the concaved surface under the overhang of a projecting upper story. (b) The splayed jambs of a flaring fireplace.
COUNTERSTROKE: A stroke or blow in return. Spenser.
CYPRIOT: A native or inhabitant of Cyprus.
CUSTODIAN: One who has care or custody, as of some public building; a keeper or superintendent.

CASH RAILWAY: A form of cash carrier in which a small carrier or car travels upon a kind of track.
CHAMBERER: 1. One who attends in a chamber; a chambermaid. [Obs.] Chaucer. 2. A civilian; a carpetmonger. [Obs.]

CLEISTOGAMIC: Having, beside the usual flowers, other minute, closed flowers, without petals or with minute petals; -- said of certain species of plants which possess flowers of two or more kinds, the closed ones being so constituted as to insure self-fertilization. Darwin.
CONCESSIVE: Implying concession; as, a concessive conjunction. Lowth.

CONGRESSMAN: A member of the Congress of the United States, esp. of the House of Representatives.

CONDUCENT: Conducive; tending. Conducent to the good success of this business. Abp. Laud.
COMPOSSIBLE: Able to exist with another thing; consistent. [R.] Chillingworth.
CANTAR: 1. A weight used in southern Europe and East for heavy articles. COPPER-FASTENED: Fastened with copper bolts, as the planks of ships, etc.; as, a copper-fastened ship.
CHORIC: Of or pertaining to a chorus. I remember a choric ode in the Hecuba. Coleridge.

CORNUTED: 1. Bearing horns; horned; horn-shaped. 2. Cuckolded. [R.] "My being cornuted." LEstrange.
CROSSHATCH: To shade by means of crosshatching.
CHEVET: The extreme end of the chancel or choir; properly the round or polygonal part.
COADUNATE: United at the base, as contiguous lobes of a leaf.
CALCED: Wearing shoes; calceated; -- in distintion from discalced or barefooted; as the calced Carmelites.
CRYPTOGRAPHER: One who writes in cipher, or secret characters.
